promptLatex: A fair coin is flipped three times. It is known that the first two flips show the same face. What is the probability that all three flips show the same face?
hintLatex: Conditioning on the first two flips agreeing leaves only four of the eight sequences.
Two of the four have all three flips equal, so the probability is $\frac{2}{4} = \frac{1}{2}$.
solutionLatex:
Three flips give $8$ equally likely sequences. The condition restricts the sample space to those whose first two entries agree.

The surviving sequences are $(H,H,H)$, $(H,H,T)$, $(T,T,H)$ and $(T,T,T)$, so there are $4$ of them, and each is still equally likely. Two of them have all three flips equal.

Therefore $P(\text{all three equal} \mid \text{first two equal}) = \frac{2}{4} = \frac{1}{2}$.
